title: Long UUP — Safe-Haven Dollar on PCE-Confirmed Fed Hawkishness + Iran Escalation
entry: Initiate $27.50–28.00 (DXY 98.5–100.5). Scale: 60% at current; add 40% on any confirmed daily close above DXY 100.00 (the regime trigger from the morning briefing) or a 30Y close above 5.10%. The DXY 100 breakout is the higher-conviction add signal.
stop_loss: $26.50 daily close (~4.5% below entry midpoint $27.75) — implies Iran ceasefire formalizes AND PCE rolls over in May data, simultaneously removing both catalysts
targets: $28.50 — DXY 101–102; Iran escalation + PCE hawkishness sustains safe-haven bid, +2.9%
$29.20 — DXY 103–104; 30Y above 5.10%, Warsh signals rate hike at June FOMC, +5.4%
$30.00 — DXY 106+; full Iran military risk premium + June FOMC hike delivery; USD structural re-rating, +8.3%
catalyst: Two independent macro catalysts converge on DXY above 100 in the 2–4 week window. First: April PCE released this morning at 8:30 AM ET is tracking approximately 3.3% core YoY (consensus), reaffirming Fed hawkishness under Chair Warsh with a June 16–17 FOMC where the 8–4 hawkish vote baseline implies a live hike discussion. Persistently above-target inflation directly supports the dollar through the interest rate differential channel. Second: the White House dismissed Iran's draft peace agreement as a 'complete fabrication' today, reinforcing that the US-Iran military exchange is ongoing and unresolved. Safe-haven dollar demand is building with DXY at 99.24 — within 76 basis points of the 100 trigger that the May 28 morning briefing flagged as the risk-off regime confirmation level.
thesis:
UUP (Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund) provides clean long exposure to the DXY through ICE US Dollar Index futures, weighted primarily to EUR/USD (57.6%), JPY/USD (13.6%), GBP/USD (11.9%), and three other G7 currencies. When DXY breaks above 100 on a daily close, the morning briefing's regime framework identifies it as a risk-off signal — which is typically associated with further dollar demand. The two-catalyst setup today is unusual: normally inflation (hawkish rates = strong dollar) and geopolitical crisis (safe-haven demand = strong dollar) don't hit simultaneously. They are today.

The rates channel: April PCE at approximately 3.3% core (vs. 3.2% in March) means inflation is not rolling over. Warsh's first FOMC on June 16–17 inherits an 8–4 hawkish voting bloc and a PCE print that stays above 3%. The Fed Funds futures market is pricing approximately 63% probability of a year-end rate hike. Rate differentials favor the USD over EUR (ECB on hold), JPY (Bank of Japan still at 0.1%), and GBP (Bank of England pausing). Every 10bps widening in the US-EU rate differential historically produces approximately 0.8–1.0% DXY appreciation. A Fed hike at June or September FOMC would be a meaningful catalyst for DXY 103–106.

The geopolitical channel: Iran's fabricated peace deal document — dismissed by the White House as 'a complete fabrication' — represents a new escalation vector. Not only are the two sides conducting military exchanges, but Iranian state media is now distributing misinformation about ceasefire progress, suggesting Iran may be playing for time or attempting to destabilize the negotiation framework. This pattern of behavior (military strikes + propaganda ceasefire narratives) is associated with sustained, unresolved conflicts. Sustained conflicts drive safe-haven USD demand from global investors repatriating risk capital into dollar-denominated assets.

The trade is sized small (2%) because UUP's upside is capped by the ETF's structure (linear exposure, no leverage) and the macro outcomes are not binary enough to justify larger conviction. The 2.9–8.3% target range reflects realistic DXY movement in a 2–4 week window without a structural regime break. This is a macro hedge to the long-equity book — dollar strength is negatively correlated to international equity positions (EWY) and mildly negatively correlated to risk-on equities (NVDA, AMD) in a risk-off regime. UUP adds diversification to a book that is predominantly long AI/tech with directional USD-neutral exposure.
bull_case: June FOMC delivers a rate hike (25bps); DXY immediately moves to 101–103; UUP to $28.50–29.20. Iran-fabricated deal narrative further undermines ceasefire confidence; Brent approaches $97–100; risk-off USD demand accelerates. 30Y yield closes above 5.10% on a persistently hawkish Fed signal. UUP to $30 within 4 weeks. Tail: a G7 ally formally requests bilateral currency support arrangements — indirect signal of DXY regime shift above 103.
bear_case: Iran ceasefire formalized despite the fabrication-denial cycle; Brent collapses to $82–85; global risk-on trade drives capital out of USD into equities and commodities. PCE May data (released ~June 26) shows a deceleration to 2.9% core; Fed signals patience at June 17; DXY falls to 97–98. UUP drops to $26.50 stop. Alternatively: Japanese yen intervention above 155 ¥/$ strengthens the JPY component of DXY calculation, creating an odd path where DXY falls despite US rates staying elevated.
invalidation: $26.50 daily close (DXY ~97.5), OR Iran ceasefire formally announced with Hormuz reopening timeline, OR Fed June 17 press conference is explicitly dovish (Warsh signals 'no hike through year-end')

outcome.outcome_label: Thesis broken — Iran ceasefire signed with Hormuz timeline
outcome.note: Primary invalidation condition met verbatim: 'Iran ceasefire formally announced with Hormuz reopening timeline.' The Islamabad Declaration signed June 14 with explicit Hormuz reopening language removes both UUP catalyst pillars simultaneously — the safe-haven Iran-escalation dollar bid and the dollar-favorable DXY-above-100 regime. DXY at 99.52 on June 15 and falling structurally (Iran deal dollar-negative). UUP estimated at $27.45, near-flat from entry — the low-conviction, small-size discipline limited the damage to a negligible -0.8%.
